g.text: An operator describes an event in their own words.
The service turns the description into an evaluation
plan, runs the plan over each new clip, and stores a
verdict with the frames that support it.
Operators review long stretches of video to find a few events.
A rule written as code needs an engineer for every change.
A reviewer watches hours of footage to confirm a few seconds
A verdict without its frames cannot be checked a month
A model update can quietly change what a trigger means.
The operator writes the event; the
service plans it, runs it on every clip, and
keeps the frames that decide it.
Each trigger compiles to an evaluation plan
with a version. A verdict records that version, so a changed plan
shows in the history and is never applied silently.
The API returns once a job is
queued, and a slow clip never holds an operator request open.
YOUR ATTENTION GOES HERE, AND ONLY HERE
You confirm each new or changed
comes back with its frames and plan version.
every active trigger and waits for your approval.
work moves, in the colour of the actor that sends it
reads or writes the verdict store
one trigger, from description to stored verdict
a lane for each actor; time runs left to right
what the service asks of its operators
A plan change never reaches a running trigger until an operator approves it.
The worker reads the approved version only.
Evidence frames are stored as references into the clip, never copied.
The evaluator holds no credentials for the verdict store.
The blocked line in view 3 is an IAM binding, not a convention.
Out of scope: live streams, identifying people, and training a model per customer.
The service evaluates finished clips with one shared model.
Each flag on the drawings marks where its note applies.
the pieces, and why each exists
balloons key the drawing to the parts list
what the service is made of, and why each part exists
verdicts without an engineer in the loop.
One authenticated entry point; the API
Turns a description into a versioned
plan and refuses to queue a plan
The API returns once a job is queued,
so a slow clip never holds a request
A clip is evaluated only once it is
complete, and the arrival event names
Clips are independent, so a failed clip
Reads frames against the plan, and has
no write path to the store.
Every verdict keeps its evidence frames
and the plan version that produced it.
Verdict review in the console: clip, evidence frames, verdict and plan version
Balloons key the drawings to the parts list, flags to the general notes, diamonds to the attention items in the title block.
